source: NCERT Class XI, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 1), Ch. 4 (Post-Mauryan Trends in Indian Art and Architecture).

sections.heading: 1. Context (c. 2nd century BCE – 3rd century CE)
points: After the Mauryas, dynasties like the **Shungas, Kushanas, Satavahanas and Kshatrapas** patronised art.
**Stupas, chaityas and viharas** developed; **Buddhist, Jain and Brahmanical** themes flourished.
Distinctive **schools of sculpture** emerged.

sections.heading: 2. Stupas and Their Decoration
points: **Stupa** parts: **anda (dome), harmika, yashti/chhatra (umbrella), medhi, vedika (railing), toranas (gateways), pradakshina path**.

The **Sanchi Stupa (MP)** — the finest; famous for its carved **toranas (gateways)** depicting Jataka tales; the Buddha shown through **symbols** (footprints, wheel, empty throne, bodhi tree) — aniconic phase.
**Bharhut and Amaravati** stupas — rich narrative relief sculpture; Amaravati (Andhra) known for its distinctive marble reliefs.

sections.heading: 3. Schools of Sculpture
points: **Gandhara school** (northwest) — strong **Greco-Roman (Hellenistic)** influence; grey schist; Buddha with wavy hair, muscular realism, drapery folds.
**Mathura school** (UP) — indigenous; **red sandstone**; Buddha shown robust, with a shaven head/spiritual expression; also Jain and Brahmanical images.
**Amaravati school** (Andhra) — white marble/limestone; narrative panels, graceful slender figures.
Both Gandhara and Mathura began depicting the **Buddha in human form** (iconic phase).

sections.heading: 4. Rock-cut Caves
points: **Chaitya** = prayer/worship hall (with a stupa inside); **Vihara** = monastery/residence for monks.
**Karla, Bhaja, Nasik, Kanheri** — rock-cut Buddhist caves of western India.
The **Karla chaitya** is the largest and finest early chaitya hall.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Sanchi Stupa = famous toranas (gateways); Buddha shown by symbols (aniconic).
Gandhara school = Greco-Roman influence, grey schist; Mathura = red sandstone, indigenous.
Amaravati school (Andhra) = white marble narrative reliefs.
Chaitya = prayer hall; Vihara = monastery.
Karla = largest early chaitya hall (western India).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Gandhara = Greco-Roman influence (grey schist)**; **Mathura = indigenous (red sandstone)**.
**Chaitya = worship hall**; **Vihara = monastery** (do not swap).
At **Sanchi**, the Buddha is depicted through **symbols** (aniconic phase).
The **Amaravati** school used **white marble/limestone** (Andhra).
